title: Investment Tracker: A Private View of Lots and Returns
author: Jason Lamb
excerpt: A private portfolio dashboard that separates investment performance from broker-reported tax basis and reviews imports before saving.

cover.alt: Illustrated private financial ledger, portfolio chart, and lock without account figures

content_html:
Investment Tracker organizes share purchases, sales, dividends, splits, and price observations into a private portfolio view. It uses central site authentication and keeps each person's records in separate server-side storage.

The dashboard distinguishes investment performance from broker-reported tax basis. Cash paid for purchases remains the basis for performance calculations, while a later broker statement can supply a separate tax-basis correction for a sale. That distinction prevents a tax adjustment from silently rewriting the history of money invested.

Imports begin with a preview. The tracker parses a report, identifies exceptions by ticker, and asks for explicit resolution where sale lots or corporate actions are ambiguous. A preview does not save records. The import path validates again before writing and avoids treating missing price information as a zero value.

The repository contains application code and synthetic test records, not personal brokerage statements or live portfolio data. The hosted app requires a permitted account; it is a personal record and reconciliation tool rather than a source of investment advice or tax determinations.
